comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's operations and suppliers are subject to complex and increasingly stringent U.S. and foreign environmental regulations regarding materials, pollutants, and waste, including restrictions in the EU and China on materials like lead and energy consumption limits for electronics.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose that their semiconductor manufacturing and operations are subject to specific environmental regulations concerning the use of hazardous substances, pollutant discharge, and product chemical content. Both companies explicitly highlight regulatory restrictions in the European Union and China regarding the use of lead in electronic products as a key compliance driver affecting materials composition and manufacturing processes.

sentences.text: Our semiconductor manufacturing operations and research and development involve the use of hazardous substances and are regulated under international, federal, state and local laws governing health, safety and the environment.

We are also regulated under a number of international, federal, state and local laws regarding recycling, product packaging and product content requirements, including legislation enacted in the U.S., European Union and China, among a growing number of jurisdictions, which have placed greater restrictions on the use of lead, among other restricted substances, in electronic products, which affects materials composition and semiconductor packaging.

Our operations and properties are subject to various United States and foreign laws and regulations, including those relating to materials used in our products and the manufacturing processes of our products, discharge of pollutants into the environment, the treatment, transport, storage and disposal of solid and hazardous wastes and remediation of contamination.
For example, the European Union (EU) and China are among a growing number of jurisdictions that have enacted restrictions on the use of lead and other materials in electronic products.

comparisons.peer_summary: Micron proactively manages environmental compliance and sustainability, conforming its wafer fabrication facilities to the ISO 14001:2015 standard to ensure continuous performance improvement.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and MU both address environmental compliance in semiconductor manufacturing, specifically noting regulations on the use of raw materials, chemicals, and waste management. AVGO cites general laws regarding health, safety, and the environment including chemical use restrictions, while MU details a proactive approach to these same areas (raw materials, chemicals, waste disposal) aligned with ISO 14001:2015 standards.

sentences.text: Our semiconductor manufacturing operations and research and development involve the use of hazardous substances and are regulated under international, federal, state and local laws governing health, safety and the environment.

These regulations include limitations on discharge of pollutants to air, water, and soil; remediation requirements; product chemical content limitations; manufacturing chemical use and handling restrictions; pollution control requirements; waste minimization considerations; and treatment, transport, storage and disposal of solid and hazardous wastes.
Manufacturing and sales of our products are subject to complex and evolving federal, state, local, and foreign environmental, health, safety and product laws and regulations and expectations.

We approach environmental compliance and sustainability proactively to ensure we meet applicable government regulations regarding use of raw materials and chemicals, discharges, emissions, climate change and energy use, and waste disposal and management from our manufacturing processes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Compliance with various governmental regulations, including those regarding IP, taxes, data privacy, AI, and environmental standards, could increase costs and have a material adverse impact on Nvidia's business and financial condition, though such compliance has not had a material effect on capital expenditures or operations to date.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both disclose that environmental regulations are part of the broader governmental compliance landscape for their operations. AVGO provides specific details on hazardous substance regulations in manufacturing (lead, waste, discharge), whereas NVDA states generally that compliance with environmental requirements could increase costs and impact operations, while noting that to date it has not had a material effect on capital expenditures.
